mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in TRANSIT below -10 reflects broad avoidance of shared mobility and predicts a continued decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks because retail trips depend on the same transit network; this drag lowers the four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -10 in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Household stockpiling pushes GROCERY_PHARM above +5, diverting discretionary spending and trip frequency away from RETAIL_REC, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks and the four-week mean is lower than the last four.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +5 in any weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of RESIDENTIAL above +2 and WORKPLACES below 0 indicates home confinement that removes commute-linked retail trips; this interaction drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > +2 and WORKPLACES < 0 in the same week
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL > +2 and WORKPLACES < 0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, TRANSIT below -10 signals enforced reduction in non-essential movement; PARKS declining below 0 confirms outdoor recreation suppression, which drags RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: In a tightening-restrictions regime with TRANSIT below -10, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of PARKS below 0 and TRANSIT below -10 shows simultaneous collapse in outdoor and shared mobility; because retail-and-recreation trips share these access modes, RETAIL_REC falls over the next week and lowers the four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS < 0 and TRANSIT < -10 in the same week
failure_condition: When PARKS < 0 and TRANSIT < -10, RETAIL_REC in the next week is higher than the prior week and the four-week mean does not fall.

mechanism_narrative: A WORKPLACES drop below -3 signals a telework shift that removes weekday commuter footfall from retail districts; this behavioral change lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -3.

mechanism_narrative: The normal March seasonal lift in PARKS and outdoor leisure is absent because PARKS has fallen from +4.6 to -5.1 over four weeks; without that seasonal tailwind, RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is lower than the last four.
failure_condition: PARKS returns to positive values and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline of TRANSIT below -10 and WORKPLACES below 0 reflects policy-driven restrictions on movement and gatherings; this policy regime forces RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks and keeps the four-week mean below the last four.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -10 and WORKPLACES < 0 in the same week
failure_condition: When TRANSIT < -10 and WORKPLACES < 0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days.
